issues.legal_issue: A person cannot establish an infringement of a fundamental right through an Article 32 petition when the claimed right depends on an underlying status or entitlement that a competent authority has finally determined against that person, unless that determination is shown to be void or is otherwise set aside.
material_facts: The petitioner’s husband transferred his interest in land to her.
After notice was issued to the petitioner and her husband, the competent authority declared the husband an evacuee and the land evacuee property.
The petitioner appeared in response to the notice and challenged the determination on its merits before the appellate and revisional authorities, but those challenges failed.
The petitioner’s application for restoration of the property was also rejected.
The petitioner did not obtain a decision setting aside the Custodian-General’s determination through an appropriate challenge, and the determination became final.
The petitioner’s claims under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 depended on establishing that the land was not evacuee property.

The petitioner alleged procedural defects in the notice but did not raise a jurisdictional objection during the proceedings before the authorities; the Court found no jurisdictional defect and no constitutional challenge to the relevant law.
issues.conclusion: The Article 32 petition was incompetent because the final determination by competent authorities negated the right on which the claimed fundamental-right infringement depended, and that determination had not been shown to be void or otherwise set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Article 32 provides a remedy for enforcement of fundamental rights, but where a competent authority has finally determined an underlying question so that the alleged right does not exist, its infringement cannot be asserted under Article 32 while that determination stands, unless the determination is a nullity or is otherwise got rid of. A challenge to the correctness of the determination on its merits must be brought through an appropriate proceeding. The Court applied Sahibzada Saiyed Muhammed Amirabbas Abbasi v. State of Madhya Bharat, [1960] 3 S.C.R. 138. It considered the claims under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 and the determinations under sections 2(d) and 2(f) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950; section 28 did not remove the constitutional jurisdiction under Articles 32, 136, 226 or 227, but the final determination still meant that no infringement was established on these facts.

rule.if: art32_fundamental_right_petition and competent_authority_decided_underlying_entitlement and decision_is_final and claimed_right_depends_on_that_entitlement and jurisdictional_nullity_not_established and decision_not_otherwise_set_aside

predicates.art32_fundamental_right_petition: The proceeding is a petition seeking enforcement of a fundamental right under Article 32.
predicates.competent_authority_decided_underlying_e: An authority competent to decide the matter determined an underlying status or entitlement on which the claimed right depends.
predicates.decision_is_final: The determination has become final in the proceedings available to challenge it.
predicates.claimed_right_depends_on_that_entitlemen: The asserted fundamental right depends on the existence of the status or entitlement decided by the authority.
predicates.jurisdictional_nullity_not_established: The petitioner has not established that the authority’s determination is void for want of jurisdiction.
predicates.decision_not_otherwise_set_aside: The determination has not otherwise been set aside through an appropriate proceeding.
predicates.art32_claim_not_maintainable: The claimed infringement cannot be pursued through the Article 32 petition while the final determination stands.

issues.definition: When an Article 32 petition depends on an entitlement finally denied by a competent authority, and the determination has neither been shown void nor set aside, the claimed infringement cannot be pursued through that petition.
